markdown_report:
### Insights and directions

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Users reject broad associations lacking current evidence; candidate attention could select more specific history. Compatibility remains unobserved. (2) Distant incidental events outweigh recent repeated interests; a short causal window limits interference. It can also discard durable preferences. (3) Electronics has 10.88% sampled training reversals and a −0.0915 tenth-percentile margin. These motivate discrimination experiments, not claims of validation improvement.

**Literature insights.** (1) DARE separates attention and representation embeddings; FPMC/FOSSIL establish directional transitions. Their combination here is incremental. (2) DIN uses unnormalized MLP weights, unlike this softmax-cosine adaptation. Query-Key Normalization motivates scaling cosine logits to avoid weak selectivity. (3) gSASRec supplies a cheaper-inference objective alternative. Sampled-metric and selection-bias studies limit conclusions from validation gains.

### Framework

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Task-specific opportunity |
|---|---|---|
| Evidence selection | DIN; DARE | Candidate-specific recent evidence |
| Relation scoring | FPMC; FOSSIL; TransGAT | Separate directional source/target factors |
| Discrimination | gSASRec; R2NS | Improve confusing comparisons |

### Candidate ideas and assessments

Scores are 0–10; difficulty increases with implementation burden. Each cell states a positive and a limitation.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Bounded recent candidate attention** | 3: focused hybrid; established ingredients | 6: modular; sparse transitions | 7: targets broad/distant associations; no compatibility guarantee | 6: discriminative branch; unverified | 6: small architecture; costly catalog scoring |
| B. Sixteen-negative gBCE | 2: established; little novelty | 7: reusable; dataset dependence | 4: finer ranking; no intent mechanism | 8: targets separation; false negatives | 3: encoder retained; sampler changes |
| C. Warm-start stochastic hard negatives | 3: practical adaptation; established curriculum | 6: informative comparisons; noisy supervision | 5: distinguishes alternatives; fulfilled needs unresolved | 8: targets confusion; instability | 5: bounded mining; extra cost |

### Selected idea: A

At 10% progress, retain the minimal architectural hypothesis, with B as a future objective comparison. Candidate-conditioned selection targets **broad associations lacking specific evidence**; a ten-event causal window targets **distant incidental interactions outweighing recent repeated interests**. Directional values target weak Electronics separation. These are mechanisms to test; completed needs and redundant substitutes remain unresolved.

Use independent attention/source/target tables, normalized vectors, fixed cosine multiplier √32, recency bias lag·log(0.8), and a residual bounded by ±1. Without scaling, the nine-lag recency penalty exceeds cosine’s entire range; scaling permits candidate evidence to overcome that ordering. Neither scaling nor attention establishes explanation fidelity.

Compare baseline, recency-only directional pooling, and candidate attention with identical losses, windows, epochs, and declared budgets. Selection alone adds parameters, so capacity remains confounded. Preserve routing, seeds, splits, environment epochs, predictor serialization, and complete-scorer diagnostics.

Select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. One changed hit moves macro HR by 0.125 points; paired intervals, when available, condition on fixed users/candidates/models and do not correct adaptive selection. Report full-catalog latency: chunking bounds memory, while candidate attention retains O(MKd) work. No gains or remaining-budget figures are assumed.

idea.description: Add a bounded candidate-conditioned directional residual to each dataset’s SASRec. Select evidence from the ten most recent valid prefix events using an independent attention embedding table, then score selected evidence with separate source-value and candidate-target tables. Preserve the baseline encoder, objective, optimizer, and negative sampling in the initial comparison. Strengthen the previous specification by scaling cosine attention logits, defining reproducible controls and scoring interfaces, and accounting for full-catalog cost.
idea.motivation: The idea explicitly targets two user-facing failures: broad associations without specific current evidence, and distant incidental interactions outweighing recent repeated interests. Candidate-specific selection and a restricted causal window provide corresponding inductive biases, although either can fail. Separate directional values also target Electronics’ weak sampled training discrimination: 10.88% ranking reversals and a −0.0915 tenth-percentile margin. Mildly positive base-embedding cosine alignment is not evidence of collapse and does not motivate a collapse penalty. Compatibility, fulfilled needs, redundant alternatives, and satisfaction remain unresolved because their labels are unavailable. Originality remains 3/10; future potential is revised from 7 to 6 because the approach overlaps substantially with DARE and incurs candidate-dependent inference work. Code difficulty rises from 5 to 6 because diagnosis compatibility, scoring shapes, and full-catalog execution require substantial care.
idea.implementation_notes:
Prespecify K=10, branch dimension d=32, normalization epsilon 1e-6, fixed cosine multiplier g=sqrt(32), recency factor 0.8, and fixed residual coefficient alpha=1.0. These are engineering hypotheses, not established optima. Relative to the previous report, multiplying only cosine by g deliberately changes its strength relative to recency. With g=1, the nine-lag penalty is approximately 2.008, exceeding cosine’s full range of 2; an oldest maximally similar event cannot outrank a newest maximally dissimilar event. Scaling the entire logit would preserve that ordering. QKNorm motivates considering a multiplier but does not establish sqrt(32) as optimal here. Do not add a temperature or recency sweep to this initial comparison.

Use independent trainable attention A, source S, and target T embedding tables with padding index zero. Initialize nonpadding rows independently from Normal(0, 1/d), where 1/d is the variance, yielding expected squared row norm one; explicitly zero padding rows. Normalize retrieved vectors as x/max(||x||_2, epsilon). This avoids deliberately tiny initial norms, although normalization gradients still depend on raw norms. Compute attention logits g*cos(A_i,A_j)+lag*log(0.8), and directional values cos(S_i,T_j). Their attention-weighted average lies in [-1,1], bounding the added score by alpha. Mask padding after transformations. Implement all-masked rows by returning zero directly, avoiding softmax over entirely negative-infinite logits. Candidate item zero receives no residual. Repeated events retain distinct positions; this is not a learned measure of semantic recurrence.

At training position t, gather at most ten valid events at positions at or before t, including sequence[t]. Assign lag zero to the newest valid event and increasing integer lags to older valid events. In normally left-padded contiguous sequences this matches positional lag; explicitly handle internal padding if present. Neither the next-item target nor a future suffix enters this window. Compute candidate attention separately for positive and negative targets, and exclude padded positive positions from loss. An observed repeated interaction may be a legitimate target; do not newly mask such targets or change baseline negative sampling for this experiment.

Construct and initialize the branch after the baseline inside an RNG-preserving context, including applicable CUDA RNG state. The unchanged baseline configuration bypasses all branch construction and optimizer registration. Keep the baseline initialization order, regularization expressions, sampler, batch size, optimizer settings, and stochastic encoder operations. Include new tables in the same optimizer with its existing defaults; apply any baseline table-specific regularization only to its original parameters and add no new explicit branch penalty. Record these settings in saved configuration rather than assuming seeds alone preserve equivalence. The branch has no stochastic forward operations.

Prespecify exactly three configurations: unchanged SASRec; a directional residual with weights proportional to 0.8^lag and no attention table; and the same residual with candidate-conditioned attention. Both residual configurations use identical S/T initialization, dimensions, windows, coefficient, normalization, encoder settings, training objective, and negative sampler. Attention adds (number_of_items+1)*32 parameters, so this comparison measures the combined effect of selection and extra capacity. It does not isolate selection at matched capacity. Wider SASRec, wider pooling, independent learned pooling, tied versus separate S/T, tied versus independent A, uniform pooling, and last-item pooling are future controls requiring retraining and equal tuning allowances. Do not silently add them to the current search.

Obtain actual remaining GPU budget from existing host accounting at execution time; no remaining amount is supplied here. All previous and new training, validation, diagnostics, debugging, and failures count toward the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. Before additional runs, reserve 20% of the actual remaining budget for diagnostics and failures and divide the remainder equally among the three configurations, including any required baseline rerun. Use charged baseline timing to freeze a common epoch cap that fits each allocation, never exceeding int(os.environ.get('SASREC_EPOCHS', '200')). Reuse a previous baseline only when architecture, initialization, data processing, training schedule, and completed epoch cap match exactly. If allocations cannot support a common comparison across all four categories, report that limitation instead of claiming a completed experiment. Select only final common-epoch checkpoints; avoid extra checkpoint or hyperparameter selection. The largest unrounded host macro validation HR@10 wins, with baseline preferred on ties and recency-only pooling preferred on remaining ties.

Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl with original routing, splits, preprocessing seed 0, and training seed 42. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Execute training on one GPU. Do not access hidden test files, alter the host evaluator, fetch pretrained weights, or add datasets. Contrary to the generic metadata examples in the input, reviews, ratings, product categories, prices, stores, and simulator traits are unavailable. Titles, descriptions, and timestamps are permitted but unnecessary for this first experiment.

Candidate-conditioned attention generally cannot be reduced to a single candidate-independent dot product. Make log2feats(sequence) return a documented feature bundle containing encoder features, recent item IDs, validity masks, and lags. Adapt all existing consumers, including diagnostics, rather than assuming the former tensor interface remains valid. Preserve predict_score(features, items) with a documented default: rank-3 encoder features use aligned B×L target scoring, and rank-2 final-prefix features use B×C candidate-list scoring. If additional modes are needed, expose an explicit optional mode argument; never infer semantics solely from B×L versus B×C item shapes, since L and C may coincide. For candidate lists, select the final valid prefix explicitly; an empty sequence has a zero branch output and follows the baseline’s documented base-score handling.

Cache recent normalized A/S vectors once per prefix and score candidates in fixed chunks of 256, retaining only running top recommendations when full-catalog output does not require all scores. Use all unseen catalog items for the twenty simulator users, five per category; chunking must not become approximate retrieval or candidate pruning. Mask seen training-history items according to the native simulator contract. Complexity is O(MKd) for the branch, versus O(MH) for baseline catalog scoring after encoding. Chunking limits memory but does not reduce total work. Record model parameter counts, charged GPU time, peak GPU memory, and end-to-end full-catalog recommendation latency for the required twenty users. Final held-out inference remains separately recorded by the host as specified.

Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, with view.model referencing the actual trained nn.Module and view.item_emb the baseline item embedding. Compute margins through the complete scorer under eval/no_grad, restoring the original training mode afterward. Keep base-table cosine measurements explicitly labeled as directional alignment rather than whole-model collapse. Preserve empty category breakdowns because item categories are unavailable. On the same bounded diagnostic batches, record attention entropy, effective attended-history count, raw table norm summaries, residual-score distribution, and residual-to-base score scale; label unavailable attention metrics for baseline or recency-only configurations. Monitor branch gradient norms during already scheduled training steps rather than running extra optimization. None of these diagnostics replaces validation HR@10.

Update the predictor writer to contain the identical architecture and serialize architecture version, baseline configuration, all branch state, initialization-independent inference settings, K, d, epsilon, g, recency factor, alpha, feature-bundle contract, and dataset routing. Verify score agreement before and after reload, aligned-versus-single-candidate scoring, candidate-chunk equivalence, empty-history behavior, padding invariance, score bounds, and prefix causality on public histories. Identical-history source/target asymmetry is learned rather than guaranteed; symmetric attention pair scores plus causal windows do not establish a complementary relation.

To detect reliance on attention, optionally replace candidate attention queries with a deterministic permutation of candidates on the existing diagnostic batch while preserving each candidate’s target vector; alternatively use recency-only weights in the fitted attention model. Report score changes and margins descriptively. These inference interventions do not substitute for retrained controls and cannot prove semantic evidence selection. The branch can learn popularity, common transitions, frequent-item hubs, or spurious associations. Restricting the window can erase older recurring preferences, and softmax always allocates unit mass over nonempty histories even when no event supports a candidate. Bounded values limit magnitude but do not provide confidence-based abstention. Lexical grounding, suppression states, and confidence gates remain future hypotheses.

Preserve the pinned validation protocol: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight macro HR@10. One changed hit moves category HR by 0.5 percentage points and macro HR by 0.125 points. If the unchanged host exposes per-user hits on identical candidate sets, jointly resample user indices across models within each category for 10,000 replicates using a separate NumPy generator seeded 42; recompute macro differences and report percentile 95% intervals, category differences, and discordant-hit counts. Otherwise state that paired uncertainty estimates are unavailable; do not modify or reproduce the evaluator to obtain them. Intervals condition on fitted models, observed users, and fixed candidates, exclude training-seed and candidate variability, and do not correct adaptive-search optimism. Under independent Bernoulli sampling, worst-case standard errors are approximately 3.54 percentage points/category and 1.77 points/macro; this approximation is not an uncertainty estimate for paired model differences. Sampled HR rankings can differ from full-catalog rankings. Simulator feedback from twenty users remains descriptive and must not trigger further tuning in this prespecified comparison.
idea.pseudocode:
CONFIGS = [baseline, recency_only, candidate_attention]
K, d, eps = 10, 32, 1e-6
g, decay, alpha = sqrt(32), 0.8, 1.0
freeze_budget_and_common_epoch_cap_from_actual_host_records()

for config in CONFIGS:
    for category in ORIGINAL_FOUR_CATEGORIES:
        set_training_seed(42)
        model = construct_original_sasrec()
        if config != baseline:
            with preserve_rng_state():
                initialize S, T independently with nonpadding N(0, variance=1/d)
                if config == candidate_attention:
                    initialize independent A identically
                zero all branch padding rows

        function log2feats(sequence):
            h = baseline_encoder(sequence)
            windows, mask, lag = last_K_valid_causal_events(sequence, K)
            return FeatureBundle(h, windows, mask, lag)

        function predict_score(features, items, mode=None):
            # Default: rank-3 h -> aligned B,L; rank-2 h -> candidates B,C.
            mode = documented_mode_from_feature_rank_if_unspecified(mode)
            base = original_baseline_score(features.h, items, mode)
            if config == baseline:
                return base
            values = shape_checked_dot(normalize(S(features.windows), eps),
                                       normalize(T(items), eps), mode)
            if config == candidate_attention:
                logits = g * shape_checked_dot(normalize(A(features.windows), eps),
                                               normalize(A(items), eps), mode)
            else:
                logits = shape_compatible_zeros(values)
            logits += log(decay) * features.lag
            weights = masked_softmax_returning_zero_for_empty_rows(logits,
                                                                  features.mask)
            residual = sum_over_history(weights * values)
            residual *= items.ne(0)
            return base + alpha * residual

        for epoch in range(COMMON_EPOCH_CAP):
            for _, sequence, positive, negative in original_train_loader:
                f = log2feats(sequence)
                pos = predict_score(f, positive, mode='aligned')
                neg = predict_score(f, negative, mode='aligned')
                optimize_original_loss_and_regularization(pos, neg,
                                                         valid=positive.ne(0))
        save_complete_config_state_and_routing_under_trial_directory()

    write_working_predictor_with_identical_architecture_and_chunk_size_256()
    verify_reload_shapes_padding_bounds_causality_and_chunk_equivalence()
    run_compatible_complete_scorer_diagnostics_within_reserved_budget()
    obtain_validation_scores_from_unchanged_host()

select_by_unrounded_macro_HR10_with_prespecified_ties()
# No additional tuning from training margins or simulator feedback.
# Report paired uncertainty only if unchanged host exposes paired user hits.

originality.positive: A focused SASRec adaptation combines candidate-specific recent evidence selection, independent selection embeddings, and bounded directional scoring.
originality.negative: DARE already decouples attention and representation tables; DIN conditions pooling on candidates; FPMC and FOSSIL establish directional transitions. The contribution is an incremental combination.

future_potential.positive: The modular branch supports controlled studies of evidence selection versus directional scoring and can later incorporate permitted public-text signals.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions, popularity shortcuts, forced softmax allocation, loss of durable interests, and O(MKd) catalog scoring constrain generality and practical value.

code_difficulty.positive: The encoder, loss, optimizer, data pipeline, and dataset routing remain largely intact; the added branch consists of small embedding tables and dot products.
code_difficulty.negative: Reliable causal gathering, feature-bundle migration, unambiguous scoring modes, all-masked handling, full-catalog chunking, predictor synchronization, and budget accounting require substantial implementation care.

related_work.title: Deep Interest Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
contributions: Introduces candidate-conditioned historical-interest aggregation through an MLP activation unit.
Uses unnormalized activation weights, retaining absolute activation strength.
limitations: The proposed normalized cosine softmax is an adaptation rather than a faithful DIN implementation.
Click-through prediction results do not establish sequential recommendation gains, compatibility, or current purchase intent.

related_work.title: Long-Sequence Recommendation Models Need Decoupled Embeddings
contributions: DARE independently learns attention and representation embedding tables.
Uses target-aware attention and representation interactions, providing close precedent for separating selection from scoring.
Its TWIN-4E comparison further distinguishes history and target roles.
limitations: DARE ties history and target representation roles and predicts from interaction vectors; the proposed residual instead uses separate directional source/target tables and scalar cosine values.
The proposed ten-event window omits DARE’s long-history retrieval setting, and its results do not validate this adaptation.

related_work.title: Query-Key Normalization for Transformers
contributions: Normalizes queries and keys and introduces a learned multiplier to control attention-logit scale.
Motivates addressing insufficient selectivity from bounded cosine logits.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal multiplier for this recommendation task.
The proposed fixed sqrt(32) multiplier is a variance-matching initialization hypothesis rather than the paper’s prescribed optimum.

related_work.title: Factorizing Personalized Markov Chains for Next-Basket Recommendation
contributions: Combines personalized preference and directional sequential transition scoring.
Provides precedent for adding a transition component to general preference scores.
limitations: Observed transitions do not identify complementarity, compatibility, or fulfilled needs.
Does not provide the proposed candidate-conditioned recent-window evidence selection.

related_work.title: Fusing Similarity Models with Markov Chains for Sparse Sequential Recommendation
contributions: FOSSIL combines historical-item aggregation with personalized lag-weighted sequential transitions.
Uses source/target factors, limiting novelty claims for directional residual scoring.
limitations: Its aggregation weights are candidate-independent.
Its results do not establish benefits for a bounded residual on SASRec under the pinned benchmark.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the SASRec sequential encoder and item-scoring baseline.
Encodes history once before candidate dot-product scoring.
limitations: The existing encoder can already represent recent and distant dependencies, so the proposed branch adds an inductive bias rather than an entirely missing capability.
Candidate-conditioned attention increases catalog-scoring work beyond the baseline.

related_work.title: Transitivity-Encoded Graph Attention Networks for Complementary Item Recommendations
contributions: Models behavioral direction and complement/substitute relations.
Motivates distinguishing relation scoring from general item similarity.
limitations: Required relation supervision cannot be assumed available here.
Purchase order and learned asymmetry alone do not establish functional complementarity.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Studies overconfidence associated with negative sampling in SASRec.
Motivates multi-negative generalized BCE as an architecture-preserving alternative with unchanged inference structure.
limitations: Additional negatives increase training work and may include relevant unobserved items.
It does not explicitly select recent evidence for each candidate; benefits under the pinned benchmark require measurement.

related_work.title: R2NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-up and curriculum-controlled hard-negative exposure.
Supports stochastic selection among difficult candidates rather than deterministic hardest-only mining.
limitations: Hard unobserved candidates can be false negatives.
Mining adds computational cost, implementation complexity, and additional experimental choices.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and model rankings.
Supports limiting conclusions to the supplied sampled-candidate evaluation protocol.
limitations: Does not justify changing the required host evaluator.
Cannot determine full-catalog performance of these models without appropriate measurements.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains selection-induced optimism from repeatedly optimizing finite validation estimates.
Motivates prespecified configurations, restricted tuning, and qualified winner claims.
limitations: Ordinary bootstrap intervals after selection do not remove this optimism.
Fixed seeds do not eliminate finite-validation uncertainty or search overfitting.

related_work.title: SciPy Bootstrap Documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling through shared observation indices.
Supports preserving user-level pairing when comparing fixed models on identical candidates.
limitations: A stratified four-category macro comparison requires resampling within each category.
Conditional intervals omit training-seed and candidate-sampling variability and do not correct adaptive selection.
